description: Outcome table of the execution check (core 20.2, bank-send 3.4). Every case assumes that every other check passed and the record state is authorized, so the verdict follows from execution and header_trust alone. Defaults: rail_ref is SHA-256 of the transaction named by rail_ref_of; the checker and the trusted chain have the action's chain id; T is checkpoint_height; the header at the tx height is trusted; sources are asked in list order. proof 'valid' is an inclusion proof of the answer's bytes that passes BX6 against data_hash of the trusted header at the answer's height, 'invalid' one that fails it (forms: the proofs section), 'none' an absent proof. result_proof (default state 'unavailable': no source serves block_results) is the outcome of RP1 to RP6 for block H: 'match_indexed' (root equals last_results_hash of the trusted header at H + 1 and the share proof binds the index; code is the selected result's), 'match_rebuilt' (root matches, the tx is not at share 0, and the block txs rebuild to data_hash and bind the index; code is the selected result's), 'match_uniform' (root matches, index unbound, every result has code), 'match_unindexed' (root matches, index unbound, codes differ, no source serves the block txs), 'match_rebuild_mismatch' (root matches, codes differ, the block txs served do not rebuild to data_hash), 'root_mismatch', 'header_unreachable' (H + 1 above T). Forms: the result_proof section. Cross agreement (result 'cross-confirmed') is reported only and never gives pass.

authorized.description: The signed minimal transaction of the profile vectors: the authorized action.

flipped.description: The authorized transaction with its last byte changed: it does not hash to the authorized rail_ref.

duplicate_body.description: body_bytes twice (another MsgSend first, the authorized body second), then the authorized auth_info and signature. The chain's decoder keeps the last body; BX3 refuses the repeat.

other_memo.description: A canonical TxRaw whose body has the authorized MsgSend but another commitment hash in the memo (tx.json body_memo_other_hash), with the authorized auth_info and signature.

live.provenance: Captured from a decision of the unsupported v0 drafts; the commitment hash in the tx memo is an opaque 32-byte input here. The capture is a Celestia fact and is not recaptured.

cases.description: One tx source. The proof verifies against the trusted header at H, and the block H results recompute to last_results_hash of the trusted header at H + 1. The share proof starts at share 0, which binds the index. Everything is proven; no cross source is needed.
The share proof does not start at share 0, so the index is not bound, but every result of block H has code 0: any tx of block H succeeded.

The tx is not at share 0, so its share proof does not bind the index, and the results of block H have different codes. A source serves the txs of block H; rebuilt as ProcessProposal builds the square, they give data_hash of the trusted header at H, and the tx is a normal tx at a known index. That binds the index.
The primary does not know the tx; the alternate does, with a proof, and the result is proven.
Everything is proven; a cross source reports code 5. A source that contradicts proven facts is reported and does not change the outcome.
The only tx source answers not found.
The only tx source fails (transport error, 5xx, 429 after retries).
The source answers with bytes that do not hash to rail_ref. They are not the transaction the receipt names, so they say nothing about the execution.
The bytes hash to rail_ref and the body is the authorized one, but the proof fails BX6 against the trusted header.
Primary bytes do not hash; the alternate's proof fails. Both sources are named with their faults.
The tx height is above the checkpoint T and no wait (OH4, MAY) reaches it.
The header the headers source serves at the tx height does not link to the trusted chain: that source's fault (OH6).

A header cross-check source gives another hash at the tx height than the trusted chain. Nothing tells whether the trusted header, the cross source or a fork is at fault, and none of them is about the decision: header_trust and execution are unchecked, with the distinct reason.
Proof verifies, code 0, no result proof (the sources do not serve block_results) and no cross source. The code rests on one source: never a pass.
The block H results do not recompute to last_results_hash of the trusted header at H + 1: that results source's fault.
The results root matches, but the share proof does not start at share 0 and the results have different codes, so nothing binds which result is this tx's.

No inclusion proof and no result proof; two cross sources agree on height, bytes and code 0. Agreement of sources is reported only: it never gives pass. Until v0-draft.27 this was the interim cross-confirmed pass.
Inclusion is proven, no source serves block_results, and the cross source agrees on code 0. Proven inclusion does not make agreement proof of the result.

The results root matches and the codes differ. The tx is not at share 0, and the block txs a source serves do not rebuild to data_hash of the trusted header at H: that source's fault, and nothing else binds the index.
The tx is at T, so the header at H + 1 that carries last_results_hash is above the checkpoint.
The results root matches, but the tx carries no inclusion proof: nothing binds the tx to block H, so the results of H say nothing about it.
No result proof; the one cross source is unreachable.
The source reports code 5; no result proof and no cross source.
Code 5, and the cross source agrees. Agreement of sources is not verified data, so a failed result needs the result proof for invalid.
The source puts the tx at the anchor height without a proof.
No proof; the cross source agrees on a height below the anchor. Agreement is not proof, so not invalid.
Primary: code 0 with a valid proof, no result proof. Cross: code 5. Nothing binds the code.
No proof. Primary and cross put the tx at different heights, both above the anchor.
The cross source answers with bytes that do not hash to rail_ref: that source's fault, so it confirms nothing.
The checker is configured for another chain than the action names. An auditor configuration mismatch, not a finding; no source is asked.

The trusted header at the tx height names another chain, and inclusion is not proven. Unreachable in the reference verifier (OH2 pins every header to the configured chain id); a checker tested alone must still give unchecked.
The receipt's rail_ref is upper-case hex. The receipt is gate-signed, so the malformed reference is proven; no source is asked.
The bytes hash to rail_ref, so the receipt binds them, and they are not a canonical TxRaw (body_bytes twice).
The bytes hash to rail_ref and the body is not the authorized one (another memo).
As above, with the tx height above T: the body finding needs no header, so it is still fail.
The primary's bytes do not hash (set aside); the alternate's do, and their body is not the authorized one.
Inclusion is proven in a trusted header whose chain id differs from the action's.
Proof verifies at the anchor height. The result is not proven, but the proven ordering violation is enough.
Code 5, proven by the result proof (index bound by the share proof).
Code 5, proven by the result proof; the tx is not at share 0 and the index is bound by the rebuilt square.
The tx source reports code 0, the result proof shows code 5. The proven code wins.
